Step-by-Step Audio Guided Tour: Dinner at Sycamore and Little Big Diner in Newton Centre, MA - Restaurant Tour
Tour-Category: restaurant

Stop 1: Farmstead Table

Address: 71 Union St, Newton, MA 02459

Coordinates: 42.3292, -71.1945

Type/Specialty: Farm-to-table cuisine

Specific Examples: Seasonal ingredients, cozy atmosphere, creative dishes

Orientation: You are about to embark on a walking journey through Dinner at Sycamore and Little Big Diner in Newton Centre, MA. The 2 km route from Farmstead Table to Sycamore offers a mix of bustling streets and quiet corners in this culinary haven. Along this path, you'll uncover the diverse gastronomic heritage of Newton Centre, from Fiorella's humble beginnings with Chef Rémon Karian's first restaurant at 23 years old to the 2016 establishment by Brandon Gillis and Boris Nemchenok, reflecting a commitment to neighborhood dining. These stops intertwine the threads of tradition and innovation in the neighborhood's culinary tapestry. At Little Big Diner, you'll learn how David Punch's venture revolutionized the Newton dining landscape. Then, at Fiorella's, discover how Rémon's marinara sauce became so popular it was eventually bottled and sold in grocery stores. Your first stop is Farmstead Table. Head southeast on Union St, the restaurant will be on your right after a few minutes walk. As you stand outside Farmstead Table, the aroma of freshly baked bread mingles with the earthy scent of herbs, instantly grounding you in its farm-to-table ethos. This unassuming spot in Newton Centre invites you to explore flavors that celebrate local and seasonal ingredients, with a menu shaped by Chef Chad Burns in collaboration with New England farmers.

Behind Farmstead Table's charming façade lies a story of culinary passion and urban challenge. Owner Ericka Harindranath faced a significant hurdle when the Newton Centre Pilot Plaza Project reduced local parking spaces. This project was intended to revitalize the area but inadvertently led to tension between local businesses and the city hall. Harindranath, voicing her frustration, underscored the delicate balance of running a restaurant in a bustling urban setting where every customer counts. Such challenges are not uncommon in the restaurant industry, yet they highlight the resilience and adaptability required to sustain a beloved local eatery. Farmstead Table connects to a broader narrative of culinary innovation in Newton. Dave Punch, a name synonymous with the area's dining scene, co-founded notable establishments like Sycamore and Little Big Diner. In 2016, Punch sparked what locals affectionately dubbed the 'Newton Centre ramen madness' when he opened Little Big Diner. Despite the freezing weather, residents eagerly lined up for a taste, marking a moment when the local culinary landscape shifted to embrace more diverse flavors. Punch's approach wasn’t just about adding another restaurant to his roster; it was about fostering a community and creating a dining experience that encouraged patrons to explore new tastes. Farmstead Table, open every day except Tuesday, welcomes guests from 12:00 pm to 3:00 pm and again from 5:00 pm to 9:00 pm. With a mid-range price point, it offers contemporary American cuisine rich with the freshness of New England's produce. Ready your palate for the next chapter in this culinary journey, where farm-fresh ingredients transform into bold, global flavors.


Directions: As you leave Farmstead Table, stroll down Langley Road towards Newton Centre. Continue walking until you reach Walnut Street, then turn left. Little Big Diner will be on your right-hand side, just a short walk away. Enjoy your meal!



Stop 2: Little Big Diner

Address: 1247 Centre St, Newton, MA 02459

Coordinates: 42.3257, -71.2080

Type/Specialty: Asian-inspired comfort food

Specific Examples: Ramen bowls, bao buns, retro diner vibe

Orientation: As you approach Little Big Diner in Newton Centre, the aroma of rich broth and sizzling meats greets you, a sensory invitation that stands out even in this vibrant neighborhood. Just a short walk from Farmstead Table, where you stopped earlier, this intimate eatery, with its sleek wooden façade and glowing neon sign, draws in patrons eager to experience its unique culinary offerings.

The story of Little Big Diner begins with Chef David Punch and his culinary team at Sycamore, who were captivated by the intricate flavors -style broths and noodles. The restaurant quickly gained notoriety for its refusal to take reservations, sparking long wait times and a phenomenon known locally as 'line rage'. In the Greater Boston food scene, Little Big Diner has carved out a niche, much like the television series "Halt and " did during its run from June 1, 2014, to October 14, 2017. Just as the show depicted the personal computer revolution of the 1980s, David Punch’s venture revolutionized the Newton dining landscape. Before Sycamore's opening in late 2012, the prevailing wisdom was that high-end dining wouldn't last here. The diner operates with a no-reservations policy, opening its doors from 4:30 to 9:00 PM, and serves dishes that hover around the $$ price range. It’s a place where traditional Japanese culinary techniques are infused with a creative twist, offering a taste of something both comforting and new.


Directions: As you leave Little Big Diner, head south on Langley Road. Walk past the charming boutiques and cafes until you reach Walnut Street. Take a left and continue walking until you see Fiorella's on your right. You've arrived at your delicious destination!



Stop 3: Fiorella's

Address: 187 North St, Newton, MA 02460

Coordinates: 42.3314, -71.2077

Type/Specialty: Italian cuisine

Specific Examples: Homemade pasta, wood-fired pizza, family-friendly setting

Orientation: As you stand before Fiorella's in Newton, take a moment to observe the warm and inviting atmosphere. Here, the scent of freshly baked bread mingles with the rich aroma of simmering marinara sauce, drawing you into its embrace.

Fiorella’s Cucina marks the beginning of a culinary journey that started in 2000, when Rémon Karian, just 23 years old, opened this restaurant with a vision and a modest budget. Rémon's dream was to create a neighborhood hub, a place where the community could gather over plates of authentic Italian cuisine. This was no easy task, yet Rémon's passion and commitment to quality paid off, turning Fiorella's into a beloved local fixture. The story of Fiorella’s is not just about its founder, but also about resilience and community spirit. In the wider Newton area, an unexpected event tested the local culinary scene. In 2018, an electrical fire devastated Buttonwood, a restaurant in nearby Newton Highlands, causing significant damage and requiring months of reconstruction. This incident echoed through the community, reminding everyone of the fragile nature of such beloved spaces. Yet, like Fiorella’s, Buttonwood rebuilt and continued to serve its patrons, reinforcing the tenacity and unity that defines this area. As you consider entering, know that this establishment offers a slice of history and a taste of passion, open Monday through Saturday from 11:30 am to 9 pm, and Sunday from 4 pm to 9 pm. Reservations are available, and the menu ranges from modest to more indulgent prices. Here, you’ll find an experience that resonates with the flavors of the past and the vibrancy of the present, promising a meal that lingers long after the last bite.


Directions: As you leave Fiorella's, walk south on Union Street until you reach Langley Road. Turn left onto Langley Road and continue walking until you arrive at Sycamore on the corner of Langley Road and Beacon Street. You'll spot the cozy ambiance and inviting outdoor seating area of Sycamore as you approach. Enjoy your meal!



Stop 4: Sycamore

Orientation: As you approach Sycamore on Beacon Street in Newton Centre, you're stepping into a dining space that defies expectations with its seamless blend of tradition and innovation.

Previously with Cambridge’s Ten Tables, Punch brought his culinary expertise to Newton Centre, transforming it into a destination for those seeking a culinary experience that marries French-inspired techniques with New England ingredients. This restaurant quickly became one of the hottest reservations in town, offering a menu that dances between French, American, Spanish, and contemporary flavors. The atmosphere buzzes with the energy of a bustling kitchen, where the sound of sizzling pans and the rich aroma of roasting meats fill the air. Uniquely, it allows him to enjoy Saturdays and Sundays off—a rarity in the restaurant industry. Here, Punch's ability to adapt and innovate shines through in cramped quarters, proving that great food transcends space. As you stand here, consider the culinary journey that Sycamore represents—a harmony of flavors crafted with precision and passion. Open from Tuesday to Saturday, 4:30 pm to 9:30 pm, Sycamore invites diners to experience a menu that reflects a vibrant community pulse. Reservations are recommended for this much-loved spot, offering a dining experience that is both satisfying and deeply connected to the traditions and rhythms of Newton Centre.



That's 4 stops and 2 kilometres — Little Big Diner, where David Punch's venture revolutionized Newton's dining scene and Sycamore, a culinary journey showcasing precision and passion in flavors.
